findings.title: upsampled_count() is only registered in DiscoverDataset but is enabled for the errors dataset
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to DiscoverDataset's function_converter, yet `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` in error_upsampling.py returns True whenever the request's dataset is `sentry.snuba.errors`, causing `_get_event_stats` to rewrite `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count` for errors-dataset requests. If the errors dataset's query builder does not include `upsampled_count` in its own function converter (the errors dataset is a separate dataset class and only discover.py was modified), those requests will fail with an invalid/unknown function error for every allowlisted project. Either register the function in the errors dataset's converter as well, or restrict the transform to datasets where the function is actually defined. This path is also untested — all new endpoint tests exercise the default (discover) dataset.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is computed against the closure `dataset` and original request query, not the scoped dataset/query actually executed
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, ...)`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the outer `dataset` variable and the raw `request.GET["query"]`, ignoring the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments. In the dashboard widget discover-split flow (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a rewritten query such as `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction` (errors-only). When the outer dataset is e.g. metrics_enhanced_performance, or the original query string lacks `event.type:error`, the transform is skipped even though the executed query is an error-only discover query that should be upsampled — dashboards on allowlisted projects will show under-sampled counts. The decision must be made from `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` string passed in.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated `!event.type:error` filters as error-focused queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring test `"event.type:error" in query`. A discover query like `!event.type:error` (excluding errors, i.e. returning transactions/other events) contains the substring, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True and `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`. For non-error events `sample_weight` is not populated (the helper itself documents that sample_weight doesn't exist for transactions), so the returned count will be wrong (typically 0) instead of the real event count. The check needs to parse the query's filter conditions rather than substring-match, or at least reject negated terms.

findings.title: Endpoint tests don't isolate the 60s eligibility cache, making them order-dependent
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches its result under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org_id}:{hash(project_ids)}` for 60 seconds in the shared cache, and nothing in the new test class clears it. Django test transactions roll back org/project id sequences, so consecutive test methods in this class reuse the same org id and project ids. `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` caches `True` for that key; if `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` (which mocks a partial allowlist and asserts un-upsampled counts of 1) runs afterwards in the same process with a real (non-dummy) cache backend, it reads the cached `True`, applies upsampling, and asserts against counts of 10 — failing. setUp should delete the cache keys (or the helper should be patched), and there are no tests at all for `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` itself, its caching, or `invalidate_upsampling_cache`.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code — nothing calls it when the allowlist option changes
findings.body: The docstring of `invalidate_upsampling_cache` says it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency across the system", but no code in this PR (option update handler, signal, or task) invokes it. In practice the only consistency mechanism is the 60-second TTL, so the function is misleading dead code; either wire it into the option-change path or remove it and document that only the TTL bounds staleness.

findings.title: Equations referencing count() are not transformed, mixing sampled and upsampled values in one response
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites y-axis columns; `equations=self.get_equation_list(organization, request)` is passed through untouched. A widget using yAxis `count()` plus an equation such as `equation(count() / count_unique(user))` on an allowlisted error query will get an upsampled `count()` series next to an equation computed from the raw sampled `count()`, producing internally inconsistent numbers (e.g. an "events per user" ratio computed from a count 10x smaller than the displayed count). Either rewrite count() inside equations or reject/skip upsampling when equations are present.

findings.title: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling silently swallows all errors and drops client_sample_rate of 0
findings.body: The new factory helper wraps its logic in two bare `except Exception: pass` blocks, so any structural problem with `contexts` (or an invalid sample rate value) is silently ignored and the event is stored without a sample rate, making downstream upsampled-count assertions pass or fail for the wrong reason. Additionally, `if client_sample_rate:` treats a legitimate value of `0` as absent, so a client_sample_rate of 0 never sets sample_rate. At minimum, narrow the exception handling and compare against None explicitly.
